raw_response:
I been farming this same ground thirty years. Last year worked fine so I do mostly the same. My neighbors all do similar, that way I know it works.

For the wheat, I plant it after maize comes off in October. I use that good wheat seed the dealer in town sells — everyone around here plants that kind now, the old seeds don't yield good. Before planting I spread two bags of that diammonium (DAP) per mu, that's 50 jin each bag so one hundred jin. My man helps with the plow, we turn the soil proper before sowing, not that no-till thing — I don't trust it, the ground gets hard. Then in spring when the wheat is greening up I put urea, maybe one bag per mu, that's 50 jin. Water it three times — once before winter, once when it's greening, once when the head is filling. If it don't rain I water four times. Spray for aphids and that rust sickness twice, maybe three times if the weather is wet.

For maize after wheat, I plant that hybrid seed right after wheat harvest in June, no time to waste. I put one bag of compound fertilizer at planting, then when the maize is knee-high I topdress urea, about 50 jin per mu. Summer rain usually enough but if August is dry I water once from the well. Spray once for the borer worm, sometimes twice.

I don't waste money on extra fertilizer but I rather put a little more than lose the harvest. Bad harvest means no money for the whole year.
